title: Ravens’ Jacoby Brissett can become first QB in Super Bowl era to pull off this feat vs. Chargers
content:
When Jacoby Brissett makes his Baltimore Ravens debut on “Monday Night Football” against the Los Angeles Chargers, he could become just the second quarterback — and the first in the Super Bowl era — to beat the same opponent in the same season while playing for two different teams.

He’s also aiming to become the 11th quarterback in NFL history to win starts with two different teams in the same season.

Brissett led the Arizona Cardinals to a 26-14 win over the Chargers in Week 1, passing for 277 yards and one touchdown with a 73.0 percent completion rate — just shy of his most accurate performance of the season.

If Baltimore can hand the winless Chargers their ninth straight loss, Brissett will officially enter the record books.

The Ravens traded for Brissett after starter Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley both went down with significant injuries during a blowout loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 8. Jackson is expected to miss six to 10 weeks after having thumb surgery, while Huntley is on season-ending injured reserve with turf toe.

Baltimore started undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano in a 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 9. At 4-5 and with 11 days between their next game, the Ravens turned to Brissett with the hope he can keep them in the playoff mix until Jackson potentially comes back.

Baltimore is Brissett’s seventh team since the New England Patriots selected him in the third round of the 2016 NFL Draft. He has also played for the Indianapolis Colts, Miami Dolphins, Cleveland Browns, Washington Commanders and Cardinals.

Only seven quarterbacks prior to this season have faced the same opponent twice in one year while playing for two different teams since at least 1950, per the Associated Press. The only one to go 2-0 against the common opponent was Jack Kemp in 1962, when he beat the New York Titans as the starter for both the San Diego Chargers and the Buffalo Bills.

Just last season, Joe Flacco had a chance to beat the Green Bay Packers twice with two different clubs. Flacco helped the Browns pull off an upset of the Packers in Week 3 and then faced Green Bay again three weeks later after being traded to Cincinnati. The Bengals lost that game, 27-18.

On Sunday night, Kirk Cousins will become the ninth quarterback to start against the same foe twice in a season with different teams. Cousins started in the Las Vegas Raiders’ loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 8, and he’ll face San Francisco again in Mexico City after being traded to the Minnesota Vikings.
